newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK democrats vent anger over assembly to Albright.
newsitem.headline: HK democrats vent anger over assembly to Albright.

text.p: Hong Kong's popular Democratic Party vented its anger to U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright on Sunday over Washington's plan to send a senior envoy to the swearing-in of a new unelected legislature.

Democratic Party legislator Lee Wing-tat and a number of his colleagues met Albright, who is in the territory for ceremonies marking the British colony's return to Chinese rule at midnight (1600 GMT) on Monday.
"The Democratic Party is very dissatisfied with the U.S. for its decision to send its consul-general (Richard Boucher) to the swearing-in ceremony," Lee told reporters.
"The Democratic Party feels it gives a mixed signal to Hong Kong and the world. It shows the U.S. recognises the legitimacy of the provisional legislature," he said.
Albright, who has said she would boycott the swearing-in of the Beijing-anointed provisional legislature, made no reply to the criticism, Lee added.
Democratic Party members will be thrown out of office at the stroke of midnight on June 30 when China takes back Hong Kong.
They were excluded from the provisional chamber, which will replace the current legislature elected in 1995.
Western nations have condemned China's plan, saying it was unjustified and unnecessary.
Australian Foreign Minister Alexander Downer said on Sunday that the territory's future leader Tung Chee-hwa had told him he would schedule new elections for the legislature next May.
It was the first time a specific month had been mentioned publicly for the polls.

During a reception at Boucher's home on Sunday, Albright said her refusal to attend the swearing-in of the provisional legislature "sends a clear political message that the United States is and will remain a friend to democracy in Hong Kong and elsewhere".
She said authorising Boucher's presence "does not, as some suggest, dilute the message of American support for democracy".
